subject: Trying to understand output differences between two different modeling approaches

messages.author: c9eec36a3a9e119a
messages.subject: Trying to understand output differences between two different modeling approaches
parts:
Hi All-
I'm trying to understand how I have such different results based on my modeling approach. Below, is the code and output, color coded, to show what my input and output was. The same dataset was used, same covariate included, binning, truncation, etc. My big question is the difference in observations between the two methods. Any insight? 
Thanks!

mcdsPRIMSUBDSM<-ds(ALLROCK, key="hr", order=0,dht.group=FALSE,formula=~as.factor(PrimSub)
+ ,truncation=list(left=1, right=20),cutpoints=dist.bins)

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Trying to understand output differences between two different modeling approaches
parts:
Hi Katy, hi listfolks,

From the models you sent, it looks like the left truncation was
different in the two models. The former left truncates at 1m where as
the latter at 0m (i.e., no left truncation), hence the difference in the
number of observations.

Hope this helps.

cheers,
--dave
